source_text: ἀπαρχὴν ἔσεσθαι τῶν κεκοιμημένων δευτέραν. Οὐ γὰρ ἐσομένου θανάτου, πῶς ἂν γένοιτο καὶ ἀνάστασις; Ἔστι τοίνυν οὐ ψευδοεπῆσαι λέγοντας, ὡς εἷς ὁ τοῦδε καιρὸς, καθάπερ ἔφην ἀρτίως, καὶ ἡμέρα μία, ἧς καὶ ὁ προφήτης ἐμνήσθη λέγων ὡς ἐκ προσώπου Θεοῦ, «Καιρῷ δεκτῷ ἐπηκουσά σου, καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σωτηρίας ἐβοήθησά σοι.» Γράφει δὲ καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, «Ἰδοὺ νῦν καιρὸς εὐπρόσδεκτος, ἰδοὺ νῦν ἡμέρα σωτηρίας,» καθ' ἣν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνεβίω Χριστὸς, τὸ ἀμειδὲς τοῦ θανάτου καταλύσας κράτος, ὅτε καὶ τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησίας οἰκοδόμους ὥσπερ τινὰς καὶ τεχνίτας πνευματικοὺς τοὺς ἁγίους ἀποστόλους καθίστη, λέγων, «Πορευθέντες μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, διδάσκοντες αὐτοὺς τηρεῖν πάντα, ὅσα ἐνετειλάμην ὑμῖν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.» Ἢ γὰρ οὐχὶ τοῦτο εἶναι φὴς τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὴν σύστασιν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ τί δὴ φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Τὴν διὰ τῶν ἁγίων μυσταγωγῶν παραδοθεῖσαν πίστιν, καὶ κεκηρυγμένην πολιτείαν, φημὶ δὴ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ, καὶ τὴν διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος πρὸς Θεὸν ἕνωσιν, διὰ μετοχῆς τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος. Οὕτω γὰρ ἡμῖν προσεφώνει λέγων ὁ Παῦλος, «Καὶ ὑμεῖς ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες ἐποικοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικὸς, εἰς ναὸν ἅγιον, εἰς κατοικητήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν Πνεύματι.» Πάλαι μὲν γὰρ ὡς ἐν διαφόροις σκεύεσιν ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ προεμορφοῦτο Χριστὸς, ὡς χρυσοῦν θυμιατήριον, ὡς κιβωτὸς, ὡς λυχνία, καὶ μὴν καὶ ὡς τράπεζα, καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ· ἕκαστος δὲ, οἶμαι, τῶν πεπιστευκότων, κατά γε τὸν ἐνεστηκότα καιρὸν, οἶκος καὶ ναὸς χρηματίζει Θεοῦ, Χριστὸν ἔχων ἐνηυλισμένον. Κατοικεῖ γὰρ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς πίστεως, καθὰ γέγραπται, εἷς μὲν καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς κατὰ φύσιν ὑπάρχων, εἰ καὶ νοοῖτο μετὰ σαρκός. «Εἷς γὰρ Θεὸς ὁ Πατὴρ, ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα, καὶ εἷς Κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς, δι' οὗ τὰ πάντα,» τοῖς δὲ τῆς θεότητος διαφόροις ἰδιώμασιν τὸ οἱονεὶ πολυειδὲς ἔχων ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ, καὶ διαφόρως νοούμενος. Ἔστι γὰρ ἐν ἡμῖν ὡς Λόγος Θεοῦ, καὶ σοφία, καὶ φῶς, καὶ ζωὴ, καὶ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνῆκα ὃ φής. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ὁ τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως καιρὸς ἡμῖν, καὶ τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάσεως ἡ τριπόθητος ἡμέρα, προανετυποῦτο πάλαι διὰ τὸ φάναι Θεὸν, Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ στήσεις τὴν σκηνήν. Τὸ δὲ, Καὶ ἐν νουμηνίᾳ τοῦ μηνὸς τοῦ πρώτου, χρησίμως τε καὶ ἀναγκαίως προσενηνεγμένον κατίδοι τις ἂν, ὦ Παλλάδιε. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἀρχὴ μηνὸς, ἡμερῶν ἡ ἐν αὐτῷ πρώτη, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἡ νουμηνία· οὕτως καὶ ἀρχή τις ὥσπερ αἰῶνος νέου, καὶ προεισβολὴ καινότητος χρόνων, ὁ τῆς ἐπιδημίας καιρός. «Καινὴ γὰρ κτίσις ἐν Χριστῷ· τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθεν.» Ἀναλάμπει δὲ ὥσπερ ἡμῖν ὁ μετὰ τοῦτον αἰὼν, νῦν μὲν ὡς ἐν ἐλπίσιν ἔτι βλεπόμενος, τότε δὲ καὶ παρεσόμενος
pass_a_gloss: [cont. from §3: nor even] that there will be a second firstfruit (ἀπαρχή) of those fallen asleep (κεκοιμημένων). For death not being going to be, how would there also be resurrection (ἀνάστασις)? So it is possible not to speak falsely (ψευδοεπῆσαι) when saying that one is the time of this, as I said just now, and day one, of which the prophet made mention, speaking as from God's person (πρόσωπον): 'In an acceptable (δεκτῷ) time I heard you, and in a day of salvation (σωτηρία) I helped you.' And the godlike Paul writes: 'Behold now a well-acceptable (εὐπρόσδεκτος) time, behold now a day of salvation', in which Christ came back to life (ἀνεβίω) from the dead, having dissolved (καταλύσας) the unsmiling (ἀμειδές) power (κράτος) of death, when also he was appointing (καθίστη) the holy apostles as builders (οἰκοδόμοι) and spiritual craftsmen (τεχνῖται) of the Church from the nations (ἐθνῶν), saying: 'Going, disciple (μαθητεύσατε) all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to keep all that I commanded you; and behold I am with you all the days until the completion (συντέλεια) of the age.' Or do you not say this is the constitution (σύστασις) of the Church? Pall.: What do you mean? Cyr.: The faith handed down (παραδοθεῖσαν) through the holy mystagogues (μυσταγωγοί), and the proclaimed way of life (πολιτεία), I mean the one in Christ, and the union (ἕνωσις) with God through holy baptism, through participation (μετοχή) of the Holy Spirit. For so Paul addressed us: 'And you as living stones are being built up a spiritual house, into a holy temple, into a dwelling (κατοικητήριον) of God in Spirit.' For long ago Christ was being pre-formed (προεμορφοῦτο) as in various vessels in the holy tent: as golden censer (θυμιατήριον), as ark, as lampstand, and as table and the things in it; but each of those who have believed, in the present time, is called (χρηματίζει) house and temple of God, having Christ dwelling within (ἐνηυλισμένον). For he dwells in our hearts through faith, as written, being one and the same by nature (κατὰ φύσιν), even if he is thought of with flesh. 'For one God the Father, from whom all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom all things', but having on himself the as-it-were many-formed (πολυειδές) by the various properties (ἰδιώματα) of the Godhead (θεότης), and being thought of variously. For he is in us as Word of God, and wisdom, and light, and life, and the bread living and from heaven. Pall.: I understood what you say. Cyr.: So the time of the becoming-man (ἐνανθρώπησις) for us, and the thrice-longed-for (τριπόθητος) day of the resurrection from the dead, was prefigured (προανετυποῦτο) of old through God's saying: 'On one day you will set up the tent.' And 'and at new moon of the first month' one would see added usefully and necessarily, O Palladius. For as the beginning of a month is the first of days in it, that is, the new moon; so also a sort of beginning of a new age (αἰών), and first onset (προεισβολή) of newness (καινότης) of times, is the time of the sojourn (ἐπιδημία). 'For new creation (κτίσις) in Christ; the old things passed away.' And the age after this one shines up (ἀναλάμπει) for us, now still seen as in hopes, then also going to be present [cont. §5: truly].
pass_b_english: that there will be a second firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep (1 Corinthians 15:20). For if there is to be no more death, how could there be a resurrection? So we may say without falsehood that this time is one, as I said just now, and the day is one. The prophet too mentioned this day, speaking as in the person of God: ‘In an acceptable time I have heard you, and in a day of salvation I have helped you’ (Isaiah 49:8). And the inspired Paul writes: ‘Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation’ (2 Corinthians 6:2). On that day Christ came back to life from the dead, having destroyed the grim power of death; and then he also appointed the holy apostles as builders, so to speak, and spiritual craftsmen of the Church from the Gentiles, saying: ‘Go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age’ (Matthew 28:19–20). Or would you not say that this is what forms the Church?
Palladius: What exactly do you mean?

Cyril: The faith handed down through the holy teachers of the mysteries, and the way of life that has been proclaimed, I mean the life in Christ, and the union with God through holy baptism, by sharing in the Holy Spirit. For so Paul addressed us, saying: ‘And you, like living stones, are being built up as a spiritual house (1 Peter 2:5), into a holy temple, into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit’ (Ephesians 2:21–22). For of old Christ was foreshadowed in the holy tent as though in various vessels: as the golden censer, as the ark, as the lampstand, and also as the table and what was set on it. But now, in the present time, each of those who have believed is, I think, called a house and temple of God (1 Corinthians 3:16), since he has Christ dwelling within him. For Christ dwells in our hearts through faith, as it is written (Ephesians 3:17). He is by nature one and the same, even when he is thought of together with the flesh; for there is ‘one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things’ (1 Corinthians 8:6). Yet through the various properties of his Godhead he has in himself, as it were, many forms, and he is understood in various ways. For he is in us as the Word of God, and as wisdom, and light, and life, and the living bread that came from heaven (John 6:51).
Palladius: I understand what you mean.

Cyril: So the time when he became man for us, and the much longed-for day of the resurrection from the dead, were prefigured of old when God said: ‘On one day you shall set up the tent’ (Exodus 40:2). And as for the words ‘and at the new moon of the first month,’ one can see, Palladius, that they were added usefully and of necessity. For as the beginning of a month is the first of its days, that is, the new moon, so the time of his coming among us is a kind of beginning of a new age and the first onset of new times. For ‘in Christ there is a new creation; the old things have passed away’ (2 Corinthians 5:17). And the age that follows this one dawns upon us, as it were, now still seen as in hope, but then to be present

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, continuing Cyril's turn from §3, so no speaker label. 'Firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep' = 1 Corinthians 15:20. Isaiah 49:8 matches LXX; 2 Corinthians 6:2 matches the NT. Matthew 28:19-20 quoted nearly verbatim; 'all the days' rendered 'always'. 'The grim power of death' (τὸ ἀμειδὲς τοῦ θανάτου κράτος) may echo Hebrews 2:14; not cited. Cyril attributes the 'living stones' text to Paul, but it joins 1 Peter 2:5 ('ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικὸς') with Ephesians 2:21-22 ('εἰς ναὸν ἅγιον ... εἰς κατοικητήριον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν πνεύματι'); the attribution is kept as written and both are cited. The list of tent furnishings (golden censer, ark, lampstand, table) resembles Hebrews 9:2-4; not cited. 'And what was set on it': αὐτῇ is feminine and could refer to the table or to the tent; taken as the table (the bread of the Presence, as in Hebrews 9:2). 'House and temple of God' cited to 1 Corinthians 3:16 as a clear allusion. 'Dwells in our hearts through faith' = Ephesians 3:17 (Cyril says 'as it is written'); the subject 'Christ' is repeated in English for clarity, as the Greek subject is the Christ just named. 'One and the same by nature, even when thought of with the flesh' keeps Cyril's Christological terms (κατὰ φύσιν; μετὰ σαρκός). The titles Word, wisdom, light, life are not cited (general titles); only the 'living bread from heaven' is cited, John 6:51. 'The time when he became man' renders ἐνανθρώπησις. 2 Corinthians 5:17: Cyril gives a shortened form ('καινὴ κτίσις ἐν Χριστῷ'), translated as he has it without the verse's 'if anyone is' frame. Ends mid-sentence (παρεσόμενος | ἀληθῶς); §5 resumes with 'in truth'.
